screens.prompt: In B4, join the first name in A2 and the last name in B2 with a single space between them.

hints.syntax: =CONCAT(A2," ",B2): the pieces in order, with the space as one of them.
hints.func-concat: CONCAT glues its arguments together in order. The space has to be passed in as an argument of its own.
hints.require-ref: Point at A2 and B2. Typing Ada and Lovelace gives an answer that ignores the next row.
hints.value: That is not first name, space, last name in that order. Check which cell comes first.
hints.error: Text divided by zero returns #VALUE!, and the grader rejects that formula. CONCAT takes text only, so leave the arithmetic out.

docs.explain:
CONCAT joins its arguments into one string, in the order you list them. The call =CONCAT(A2," ",B2) returns Ada Lovelace: the first name, a typed space, then the last name. The space is an argument of its own, so =CONCAT(A2,B2) returns AdaLovelace.

This sheet asks for the name in B4, built from A2 and B2. The space is the piece that goes missing, and AdaLovelace reads like a name at a glance. The grader compares the text, so a dropped character fails the answer with no other warning.

The & operator joins the same way and is shorter to type: A2&" "&B2 answers the same text. This exercise grades CONCAT because that is the function it names. Either version reads from cells, so a corrected row changes the answer without an edit.

errors.text: The joined text was used in arithmetic, as when the whole call is divided by zero.
CONCAT is typed as CONCATE, and the sheet has no function by that name.
The call =CONCAT(A2,B2) passes no separator, so the two names come out as AdaLovelace and the grader rejects it.

docs.atWork: A mailing list where first and last names arrive in separate columns and the export needs one name field.
docs.outcome: Join two cells into one string, with the space passed in as its own piece.

seo.title: CONCAT and & in Excel: join two cells
seo.description: Ada, a space, then Lovelace is the full name. CONCAT glues the pieces in order, the & operator joins them the same way, and the space is the part left out.
